Hi John — great speaking with you this morning. Thanks for the thoughtful questions on data residency and region pinning. Per our call, I wanted to recap the main points and proposed next steps so we can align with your security and ops teams: 

Summary of what we covered:
- Redwood supports region pinning per-customer (US, EU, APAC) so requests and persisted data can be kept in a chosen region.
- Cross-region failover is supported; we can configure automatic failover policy with controlled RTO/RPO based on the plan you choose.
- Backups are encrypted (customer-managed KMS available) and can be stored with geo-redundant copies.
- Audit logs and request/response logging can be retained for configurable retention windows; PII redaction options exist at ingestion.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I will loop in Aditya (our infra lead) to confirm specifics on backup replication, failover mechanics, and encryption key controls.
2) Can you share any constraints your compliance team has around cross-region replication (e.g., strict in-region-only backups, max retention for logs, or GDPR-mandated data locality rules)?
3) We’ll provide a short architecture note + SOC2 extract and a suggested MUTUAL ACTION PLAN (MAP) for pilot configuration.

Attaching an overview doc for quick reference (redwood-data-residency.pdf).

Thanks — happy to set up a 30-min follow-up with your security team this week if helpful.

Thanks Vanessa — that recap is helpful. A few clarifying questions from our side (security & infra):

1) Region pinning: If we pin to EU for production, can we still use US region for non-prod (dev/test) with separate projects/accounts? Any limitations on model variants between regions?

2) Cross-region failover: what is the expected RPO and RTO for model state (KV cache) vs. persistent logs/backups? How does failover handle in-flight requests and KV cache warming?

3) Backups: Do backups stay in-region by default? Do you offer synchronous replication to a second region (for immediate failover) or asynchronous replicas? Is there a snapshot cadence and retention policy we can configure?

4) Encryption & keys: we prefer CMK (customer-managed keys). Is KMS supported in all regions and can keys be restricted to region-only use?

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, John Davies <john.davies@acmebank.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACMEBank — follow-up on data residency / region pinning — technical details

Hi John / Vanessa — happy to clarify. Short answers first, then details below.

Short answers:
- Region pinning: Yes — customers can pin production workloads to a single region (US/EU/APAC) and run non-prod in other regions. Model catalog is consistent across regions; small variations may exist for GPU-backed or specialized runtime builds, but we surface compatible model variants automatically.
- Failover RPO/RTO: For persisted state (backups, logs) RPO depends on replication mode: synchronous replication to a paired region gives near-zero RPO, async replication is typically <15 minutes by default (configurable). RTO targets depend on plan; with our Dedicated/reserved plan we can target RTOs of 5–30 mins for full service failover.
- KV cache: KV cache is in-memory for serving instances and is warmed post-failover; we provide cache snapshotting for faster warmup in higher tiers, but ephemeral caches are expected on active failover — startup latency during warmup is a factor to account for.
- Backups & retention: Backups are encrypted and stored in-region by default. We support optional geo-replication (sync or async) to a secondary region. Snapshot cadence is configurable (hourly/daily) and retention windows are configurable per-account.
- KMS/CMK: Customer-managed keys are supported in all public regions we operate in. Keys can be restricted by region/policy as per the KMS provider (we integrate with major cloud KMS offerings).

Details / recommended config for Acme Bank pilot:
1) Production (EU pinned) + Non-prod (US): We recommend pinning Prod to EU and creating separate non-prod projects in US region. This isolates persisted logs/backups per-region and keeps production data in-region.

2) Backups & replication: For stricter in-region policies, set backups to in-region only. If you require rapid failover with minimal data loss, enable synchronous replication to a designated failover region (note: synchronous cross-region replication could add write latency). For most customers we use async replication with 5–15 min RPO and a Dedicated plan to meet RTO SLAs.

3) KV cache and service continuity: Plan for cache-warmup time post-failover. We can provide pre-warm hooks and cache snapshot restore to shorten recovery. If you need near-zero user-facing interruption, design a multi-region active-active read routing with a write-master in-region (architecture work needed).

4) Encryption & keys: We support CMKs and will accept key policies that restrict key usage to a region. For on-prem or VPC deployments we can bring-your-own-key (HSM/KMS) integrations.

5) Logging & retention: Audit and request logs are stored encrypted; retention defaults to 90 days but can be shortened/extended per contract. PII redaction can be applied at ingestion to drop or mask sensitive fields before persistence.

I’m attaching a short architecture note and the SOC2 extract per Vanessa’s email. Happy to join a session with Acme Sec if you want to walk through these details.

- Non-prod projects in US region for dev/test.

- KMS: Acme will supply CMKs in EU; Redwood will integrate and restrict key usage per policy.
